voyage.name: Viking Ship Museum and Historical Museum
voyage.content: Museum featuring the Tune, Oseberg and Gokstad Viking ships, found in burial mounds.Closed until 2027 for renovations.

voyage.name: Øyafestivalen
voyage.content: In the beginning of August every year, Oslo is housing the Øyafestivalen in Tøyenparken, an event which over the years has become a great festival for all kinds of people of all ages who enjoy rock and pop music.

voyage.name: by:Larm
voyage.content: Rock festival taking place in various venues downtown Oslo, mid-February. The lineup consists of mostly Norwegian (or Nordic) underground or rising artists along with some more established names.

voyage.name: Findings
voyage.content: EDM festival at Bislet Stadion every August

voyage.name: Inferno
voyage.content: Inferno is a metal festival taking place in various venues downtown Oslo, late March. Dating back to the mid-1980s and the forming of bands like Mayhem, Norwegian Black Metal has established itself on the international stage. Where better to experience the sheer evil energy than in the dark and cold world capital of Black Metal; Oslo?

voyage.name: Oslo Jazz Festival
voyage.content: Taking place mid-August in various venues, downtown.

voyage.name: Oslo Chamber Music Festival
voyage.content: Founded by renowned violinist Arve Tellefsen in 1989. The programme usually spans from medieval to contemporary music. Over the years artists (in no particular order) like Barbara Hendricks, Jan Garbarek, the Hilliard Ensemble, Trio Mediæval, Solveig Kringlebotn, Elisabeth Norberg-Schulz and many others have performed.

voyage.name: Musikkfest (National Music Day)
voyage.content: Free, mostly outdoors, music festival established in Oslo in 1992, as a spinoff from Fête de la Musique. Always taking place first Saturday in June.

voyage.name: Oslo Pride
voyage.content: Gay/lesbian pride festival and parade taking place all over, late June.

voyage.name: Films from the South
voyage.content: Film festival presenting movies from Asia, Africa, Middle East and Latin America. Established in 1991. Takes place in various theatres in Oslo, mid-October. Arabian Film Days late April.

voyage.name: Boating the inner Oslofjord
voyage.alt: from the port next to the Oslo City Hall and Aker Brygge
voyage.price: A valid ticket for the public transport in Oslo, the price is the same to most islands. For those who want it, there is also fjord sightseeing and a Jump On - Jump Off sight seeing boat with trips in the harbor area.
voyage.content: A relaxing break from the busy city: There are many boats and ferries that can take you to the idyllic, small islands of the archipelago in the inner Oslofjord. Activities such as fishing, swimming, sunbathing, strolling and exploring ashore the islands. To the museums at the Bygdøy peninsula is a separate all year ferry . Throughout the year the Oslofjord can be crossed by ferry B10 to Nesodden. There is also a boat

voyage.name: Royal Palace
voyage.content: The Palace is the residence and offices of the king, Norway's head of state. Council of State meetings are held there every Friday. When new members of cabinet have been appointed by the king they appear in the front of the palace for photo sessions and interivews. Building of the Palace began in 1824 and completed in 1849. The Palace sits on a small mount at the end of Oslo main street, Karl Johans gate, named after

voyage.name: Opera House
voyage.content: Norway's first entry into the top league of modern architecture. Awarded the 2008 prize for best cultural building at the World Architecture Festival in Barcelona, and the prestigious Mies van der Rohe award for best European contemporary architecture in 2009, its appearance is stunning. Shaped as a glacier or a ship, the amazing building seems to float by the inlet Bjørvika, giving a stunning impression. Climb the b

voyage.name: Oslo Cathedral
voyage.content: Oslo's cathedral is none too impressive, but has been refurbished. It was erected in 1697, and expanded in the 19th century using different coloured brick (still visible). After the terrorist attacks on Oslo in July 2011, the square Stortorget, in front of Oslo Cathedral, became the centre for afterthought and compassion. The square was fully covered by roses, greetings and mourning messages for weeks. Affiliated wit

voyage.name: Kirkeristen
voyage.content: The small, old bazaar surrounding the church is now used by artisans and craftsmen, and holds a couple of small cafes and restaurants. This building was constructed around 1850 in neo-romantic style on the site of an older butchers' bazaar.

voyage.name: City Hall
voyage.content: A monumental functionalist building in red brick. Opinions are divided if this is a pretty building, but it is certainly imposing. The austere facade has a surprising number of fine details. Open to the public, with a spectacular main hall featuring huge murals with typical Nordic social democratic themes. Other rooms are also decorated with a variety of art. There are also some displays of historical artefacts in th

voyage.name: Akershus Castle and Fortress
voyage.content: A medieval castle and fortress built in 1299, located close to the city centre. There are several excellent viewpoints to the Oslofjord and surrounding areas. The stone walls create an exciting atmosphere, and you are free to roam around in tight passages and staircases. There are two museums here, both related to Norwegian military history (see museums below).

voyage.name: Stortinget
voyage.content: It has free guided tours in English and Norwegian lasting about 45 minutes, which assemble outside the back door of the Parliament (on Akersgata). There is a limit of 30 people per tour, so be there at least 10 minutes prior to the start of a tour.

voyage.name: University of Oslo
voyage.content: The original campus and buildings of the university, completed around 1850. The buildings houses only the Faculty of Law; the rest of the university is situated at Blindern. There are occasional concerts in the magnificent Universitetets Aula, housing 11 of Edvard Munch's pictures covering more than 200 m² of wall. The room is only occasionally open to public, but is one of the most magnificent rooms in all of Norway

voyage.name: Government Building Complex
voyage.content: Regjeringskvartalet is a group of buildings housing several of the offices of the executive branch (ministries) as well as the Supreme Court. The area does not display a consistent style but instead reflects 200 years of development. The prime minister's building and the Y-building are functionalist or brutalist architecture. The Y-building has a particular layout and the facade is decorated by Picasso's drawings car

voyage.name: Nordic Bible Museum
voyage.hours: T-Wed: noon-5pm, Thu: 11am-6pm, Fri-Sun: 11am-4pm, Mon: closed
voyage.content: This is a little museum dedicated to the Bible's history, cultural influence, and main translations. The friendly tour guides will take you through their impressive collection, which spans centuries and includes a reproduction of a Dead Sea scroll page. You also get an opportunity to try writing on papyrus and vellum.

voyage.name: The Mini Bottle Gallery
voyage.content: A unique collection of mini bottles. While the bottles are small, the museum exhibits 12,500 of them from a collection of 53,000, over an area of 1,500 m².

voyage.name: The Queen Sonja Art Stable
voyage.content: A museum, art gallery and concert hall located in the former stables of the Royal Palace in Oslo. Varying exhibitions where most of the items are from the Norwegian Royal Collections.

voyage.name: Slottsparken
voyage.content: Surrounds the Royal Palace (see above) at the top of Karl Johan street. Oslo's most central park is a pleasant grass-covered area with majestic old trees. When you are in the park, don't miss Princess Ingrid Alexandra's Sculpture Park area, which contains sculptures made by children from all over Norway. Wide walkways crisscross the park. The Royal Guards have a small barrack in the park.

voyage.name: University garden
voyage.content: Pleasant park surrounding university buildings on Karl Johan street, completed around 1850.

voyage.name: Studenterlunden
voyage.content: the park in the heart of Oslo, between the parliament and the National Theatre. Fountains in the summer, an ice rink in the winter, outdoor seating and a variety of statues of famous Norwegians including Henrik Ibsen, Ludvig Holberg and Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson.

voyage.name: The Armed Forces Museum
voyage.content: Describes Norwegian military history and provides an insight into the development from the Middle Ages to the first years after World War II.

voyage.name: Hjemmefrontmuseet
voyage.content: Describes the resistance against the Nazi German occupation of Norway during World War II.

voyage.name: Oslo Concert Hall
voyage.content: One of the main venues for classical and contemporary music in Oslo. The concert hall is home of the Oslo Philharmonic Orchestra, a world-class symphony orchestra. The building is modern with a modest exterior.

voyage.name: Oslo Spektrum Arena
voyage.content: The place for great concerts, rallies and indoor sports events.

voyage.name: National Theatre
voyage.content: One of Norway's main theaters for performance of dramatic arts. The building is monumental and there are statues of several well-known Norwegian playwriters by the main entrance.

voyage.name: Det Norske Teatret
voyage.content: The largest theater in Norway where the standard language is Norwegian Nynorsk.

voyage.name: Oslo Nye Teater
voyage.content: This is Norway's most visited theater institution with four theater stages, with different locations in the city. The main stage is the largest. The standard language is Norwegian Bokmål. Rarely performances in English.

voyage.name: Chat Noir
voyage.content: Norway's oldest and most famous scene for revues and entertainment, established in 1912. Rarely performances in English.

voyage.name: Akersgata
voyage.content: A few exclusive shops like Louis Vuitton, gold smith David-Andersen, Follestad, Corso Como, Ting. The most exclusive shopping-centre in Oslo.

voyage.name: Byporten
voyage.content: A shopping centre appended to the Sentralstasjon, with a selection of Norwegian chain stores. Handy for last-minute shopping or filling up supplies on arrival, but mind the opening times, much shorter than the station's.

voyage.name: Eger
voyage.content: High-end fashion shopping in the middle of Karl Johans gate.

voyage.name: Glasmagasinet
voyage.content: Dates back to the 18th century. Here you can find souvenirs, crystal, china, fashion, kitchenware and interior design. The department store is famous for their large cosmetics section.

voyage.name: Oslo City
voyage.content: A big shopping centre just across the street from the Central station. The shopping centre focuses on young people. In the basement is Meny, one of the few full-size supermarkets in central Oslo.

voyage.name: Paleet
voyage.content: An upmarket, central shopping centre.

voyage.name: Steen og Strøm
voyage.content: One of Oslo's oldest department stores and is newly renovated and very stylish with a number of clothing shops with famous brands, a cosmetique, and an interior design floor. On top you will find an outdoor cafe with view over the city centre and the surroundings.

voyage.name: DesignTorget
voyage.address: Byporten shopping centre, House of Oslo shopping centre and Grensen 8
voyage.content: Swedish chain that showcases high quality quirky design. Worth checking out for quality gifts to bring back home.

voyage.name: Oslo Gift Shop
voyage.content: Souvenirs.

voyage.name: Living Large
voyage.content: A store for tall and large men, sizes range from 3X to 9X with decent formal and informal clothes.

voyage.name: Norway Shop
voyage.content: Greatest selection in the city of original Norwegian knitted wool sweaters.

voyage.name: Fisketorget: The Oslo Fish Market
voyage.content: Fish market of fresh fish and shellfish that has an aquarium, seafood restaurant and sushi and oyster bar.

voyage.name: Oslo Wool Shop
voyage.content: Traditional Norwegian sweaters.

voyage.name: Stormberg
voyage.content: Stores for Norway's largest brand of outdoor wear.

voyage.name: Tursenteret, Den Norske Turistforening
voyage.content: Equipment shop and good advices for hikers and cross country skiers, tour maps, booking of tourist cabins.

voyage.name: Gulating Ølutsalg
voyage.content: Largest selection of beer in the city, Norwegian craft beer from all over Norway in particular.

voyage.name: Tiger
voyage.content: An old-school record store with vinyl, CDs and some band merchandise for those into alternative music like punk, noise and all kinds of genres with names ending with "core". Also a record label and a distributor.

voyage.name: Prince Lunch Bar
voyage.content: The best baguettes downtown. Delivers lashings of filling on their almighty subs. Also chicken breast, fish and beef burgers.

voyage.name: Rådhuset Canteen
voyage.address: In the cellar of the city hall
voyage.content: The canteen is open to the public, and offers good, sumptuous meals at even lower prices than the student canteens. Not many tourists know about the place, so it can be a very quiet place to have a meal. They sell salads, sandwiches, boiled potatoes, cereal bars and other snacks. A filling box of salad (sold by weight) can cost less than 40 kr.

voyage.name: Backstube
voyage.content: Inexpensive bakery / pastry shop / breakfast place close to the Opera house. Its part of a chain of stores

voyage.name: Dovrehallen
voyage.content: Old-school beer hall serving delicious meat and potato dishes, with a rotating daily dish. Tuesdays are "Eisbein" day, be there!

voyage.name: Engebret Cafè
voyage.content: A restaurant where Ibsen, Bjørnson, Grieg and Munch all had regular tables.

voyage.name: Fiskeriet
voyage.content: If you want to eat (for local standards) affordable seafood.

voyage.name: Kaffistova
voyage.content: Kaffistova has served traditional Norwegian fare for more than a century. «Raspeball» every Thursday.

voyage.name: Oriental
voyage.content: Brilliant all-Asian restaurant with inventive dishes.

voyage.name: Restaurant Eik
voyage.content: The least upmarket of the central gourmet offerings, Eik consistently get rave reviews and doles out a fine five-course gourmet menu for around 400 kr. Fantastic. Bib gourmand award in the Michelin Guide.

voyage.name: Restaurant Eik Annen Etage
voyage.address: above the Hotel Continental in Stortingsgata
voyage.content: When Eik took over the sadly missed gourmet Annen Etage, the food actually got better and cheaper.

voyage.name: Rice Bowl Thai Cafe
voyage.content: Seems to be packed with locals at all times. Thai food is OK but a bit bland.

voyage.name: Stortorvets Gjæstgiveri
voyage.price: Rather affordable: Today's dish 189 kr lunches. Nevertheless, the dishes in the al-la-carte menu are a lot more expensive
voyage.content: Traditional dining in an older, historical building, serving Norwegian food.

voyage.name: Sabaki
voyage.content: Traditional Japanese cuisine: Of course you will get sushi, sashimi and maki, and also robbatyaki and teppanyaki.

voyage.name: Xich-Lo
voyage.content: A central, more classy Vietnamese eatery with great food.

voyage.name: Dinner
voyage.content: One of the finest Chinese restaurants in Europe. All the expensive dishes are worth it. Try their Peking Duck, which must be pre-ordered the day before, but is a true feast.

voyage.name: Gamle Raadhus Restaurant
voyage.content: Gamle Raadhus Restaurant is located in historical surroundings: Oslo's original city hall from 1641. Serves unique traditional Norwegian food, which it has since 1856. The food (lunch and dinner) is made from scratch, with the use of local Norwegian products. Expensive.

voyage.name: Restaurant Fjord
voyage.content: The best fish restaurant in Oslo, with a menu based on taseful Norwegian ingredients.

voyage.name: Statholdergaarden
voyage.content: Arguably one of Oslo's finest settings. Set in a beautiful 18th-century mansion, the combination of very friendly staff and extraordinary dishes makes it well worth its one star in the Michelin Guide. Not one to miss.

voyage.name: Theatercaféen
voyage.content: Pretending to be a classic upmarket Wiener Café with a continental menu. High prices and excruciatingly "culture-posh", food quality is disputed. However, being "the" classic café in Oslo, the experience may be worth it.

voyage.name: Andy's Pub
voyage.content: Shows most football matches on LCD TVs.

voyage.name: Bohemen (“the Bohemian”)
voyage.content: The best place to watch football (soccer) and sports in general, and to have a cheapish beer. Official Vålerenga supporter pub.

voyage.name: Brygg
voyage.content: Night out for beer enthusiasts, offers one of the most varied beverage selections in the city.

voyage.name: Cafe Fiasco
voyage.content: Classy place that is not expensive at all. Also has live music and DJs with 70 kr cover charge.

voyage.name: Dubliner
voyage.content: A nice Irish pub a little off Karl Johans gate, does a good fish and chips (and a few rounds of Guinness with which to wash it down). In Norway: Good fish? Always! Good chips? Never! Except maybe here.

voyage.name: Dr. Jekylls Pub
voyage.content: Whisky bar with wide selection. over 500 whiskies and several fantastic rums and over 60 beers on bottle.

voyage.name: Fyret Mat & Drikke
voyage.content: Intimate and lively pub and restaurant which serves unpretentious, good food. They have an outstanding collection of akevitt (akvavit), the Scandinavian potato spirit that you should check out, though you won't necessary love it unconditionally.

voyage.name: Hard Rock Cafe
voyage.content: Dealing mainly with, as the name suggests, rock nostalgia from the 1950s, this should be familiar. Pricey.

voyage.name: Heidi’s Bier Bar
voyage.content: German, Bavarian style beer bar with the party atmosphere of afterski and octoberfest.

voyage.name: Hell's Kitchen
voyage.content: Pizza and music, lots of beer and cocktails. Brilliant place that once was the heyday of hipness, a reputation it has to leave to its own basement (The Villa) and Revolver, just down the street. Still a good corner to drop into.

voyage.name: Public Gastropub
voyage.content: Oslo's largest selections of specialty beers, hearty, simple cooking.

voyage.name: Røør
voyage.content: Two floors with a large selection of beers from around the world, shuffleboards, music and a stage.

voyage.name: Sir Winston's Public House
voyage.content: English style pub and piano bar in the main street.

voyage.name: The Old Irish Pub
voyage.content: Irish pub combined with a nightclub that offers live music, big screen sports and a dance floor.

voyage.name: The Scotsman
voyage.content: Big and well known Scottish style pub in the main street. Live music.

voyage.name: The Whisky Bar
voyage.content: Pub with large selection of whisky.

voyage.name: Amundsen Bryggeri & Spiseri
voyage.content: Gastro pub and restaurant with its own microbrewery in the middle of the room.

voyage.name: Gamla
voyage.content: Rock'n'roll bar and stage in historical surroundings.

voyage.name: Last Train
voyage.content: Sandwiched between a theatre and Hard Rock Cafe this gem is easily overlooked. One of the best (and longest lasting) rock/punk/metal/indie pubs in Norway.

voyage.name: London Pub
voyage.content: The largest gay and lesbian venue in Oslo.

voyage.name: So
voyage.content: Mostly aimed at girls. Nice cosy bar which gets packed Saturday night.

voyage.name: Perminalen Hotell
voyage.price: Dorm: kr 380; Single: kr 620; Double: kr 860
voyage.content: Perminalen offers slightly higher standards at slightly higher prices. OK cafe with good, old Norwegian homely grub at nice prices.

voyage.name: Sentrum Pensjonat
voyage.price: Dorm: kr 290; Single: kr 500; Double: kr 750

voyage.name: Oslo Hostel Central
voyage.price: Dorm: kr 375-395, 10% discount with HI membership

voyage.name: P-Hotels, Oslo
voyage.content: Affordable hotel, centrally located with nice rooms. Simple breakfast delivered to your door.

voyage.name: Smarthotel Oslo
voyage.content: Affordable, central - and smart.

voyage.name: CityBox Oslo
voyage.content: Sparse and staff-light (housekeeping once a week, no reception, no TV), but cheap and very close to the central station and Carl Johans gate. Family rooms available.

voyage.name: Hotell Bondeheimen
voyage.content: Traditional Norwegian hotel for rural people in town, established in 1913. Norwegian and homely. Tasty breakfast included.

voyage.name: Best Western Karl Johan Hotel
voyage.content: Attractive 3-star hotel in the very centre of Oslo, fully modernised while keeping its character. Many rooms overlook the parliament building, and the waterfront and royal palace are within a short walk. Rooms are reasonably large for an old building, and efficiently designed. A good breakfast buffet is included.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus City Hotel
voyage.content: A relatively small but homely hotel. Both studios and rooms. The main street Karl Johans gate is just around the corner.

voyage.name: Hotel Bristol
voyage.content: As soon as you enter the lobby you will experience the unique style characterising the hotel. An air of elegance which has been maintained since the opening in 1920. Today, the hotel is owned by the chain Thon Hotels.

voyage.name: Clarion Collection Hotel Bastion
voyage.content: Unique designed boutique hotel which possibly hides some secrets.

voyage.name: Clarion Collection Hotel Folketeateret
voyage.content: Nice hotel with stylish rooms and an evening buffet that is included in the rate. Walking distance to central station.

voyage.name: Clarion Hotel The Hub
voyage.alt: Former names: Hotel Royal Christiania, Hotel Viking
voyage.content: This huge, extended hotel in the heart of Oslo was reopened in March 2019. The hotel was at first built to accommodate the 1952 Winter Olympics in Oslo. Gym, indoor pool, relaxation area, library, restaurant, bar and a large number of conference facilities. They also have rooms that are adapted for wheelchair.

voyage.name: Comfort Hotel Børsparken
voyage.content: Centrally located hotel in a low traffic street by a small park.

voyage.name: Comfort Hotel Grand Central
voyage.content: It is not necessary to wear outerwear from the station building.

voyage.name: Comfort Hotel Karl Johan
voyage.content: Almost as central to the city as it goes.

voyage.name: Comfort Hotel Xpress Central Station
voyage.content: An efficient, new kind of hotel, close to most kinds of public transport.

voyage.name: First Hotel Millenium
voyage.content: Central B&B hotel.

voyage.name: Park Inn
voyage.content: Well-equipped guest rooms in the heart of Oslo.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Scandinavia Hotell, Oslo
voyage.content: In the heart of the city centre. In this 22-story hotel you find the wellness area Lagoon, which includes a great swimming pool and a separate fitness room. The converted rooms have spectacular views of the big city and the Oslo Fjord.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Plaza Hotel
voyage.content: With 37 floors and breathtaking views of Oslo and the Oslo Fjord, the Radisson SAS Plaza Hotel is Northern Europe’s highest hotel. Great conference facilities. There is a gym, swimming pool and sauna at the health and fitness center. Suited 3 min walk from the Oslo S train station.

voyage.name: Saga Hotel Oslo Central
voyage.content: Centrally located hotel that also offers family rooms.

voyage.name: Scandic Byporten
voyage.content: Just steps from the main entrance to the main train station Oslo S, this central hotel is located.

voyage.name: Scandic Oslo City
voyage.content: Very central, 1-3 minutes walk to several types of public transport, Oslo S train station and to the main street, Karl Johans gate.

voyage.name: Scandic Grensen
voyage.content: Not far from Oslo Cathedral, Stortorget square and Karl Johans gate

voyage.name: Scandic Karl Johan
voyage.content: This hotel is within walking distance of the main public buildings and attractions in central Oslo.

voyage.name: Scandic Victoria
voyage.content: Central but little noise. Some rooms have a balcony and some have views.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Cecil
voyage.content: Just steps away from restaurants, nightlife, shopping, and entertainment options. Not far from Karl Johans gate and Aker Brygge.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Europa
voyage.content: Close to the Royal Palace and Karl Johans gate.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Opera
voyage.price: Price:See also special offers. Depends on season
voyage.content: Probably the most central hotel in Oslo.Still, it's pretty quiet there. Offers also disabled-friendly rooms.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Panorama
voyage.content: Most rooms have a balcony, beautiful views of the city and the Oslofjord.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Terminus
voyage.content: Central hotel, close to shopping, nightlife and public transport.

voyage.name: Hotel Verandi
voyage.content: 3,5 stars hotel with 170 rooms between Aker Brygge and the main street Karl Johan.

voyage.name: Amerikalinjen
voyage.content: The former iconic headquarters of the shipping company Den Norske Amerikalinje (The Norwegian America Line) was reopened as a boutique hotel in March 2019. The hotel offers comfortable rooms very central, just off the main entrance to Oslo Central Station (Oslo S).

voyage.name: Clarion Collection Hotel Savoy
voyage.content: Central and comfortable business hotel. Breakfast, afternoon sweets and an evening meal are always included.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Oslo
voyage.content: The hotel where Nobel Peace Prize winners stay when coming to Oslo for the award ceremony. Expensive and lots of services. Excellent view over main street Karl Johans gate. Grand Café, at street level, was Henrik Ibsen's daily watering hole, and is Norway's answer to Vienna's Cafe Landtmann.

voyage.name: First Hotel Grims Grenka
voyage.content: Five-star hotel which has received international acclaim. Operated by First Hotels. Member of Design hotels.

voyage.name: Hotel Continental Oslo
voyage.content: Family-run hotel has a large Vienna-style cafe (Theatercafeen) which is the place to be seen in Oslo. Outstanding service and prices to match, still considered fair value for money. Nice quiet bar with original Edvard Munch litographs.

voyage.name: Hotel Christiania Teater
voyage.content: A boutique hotel, which was designed by the architects Henry Fearnley Coll and Hack Kampmann.

voyage.name: Nobel Peace Centre
voyage.content: Includes some confronting exhibitions and an exhibit for every winner of the Nobel Peace Prize. Included in the Oslo Pass. See also Nobel tourism.

voyage.name: Henrik Ibsen Museum
voyage.content: This museum is a treat. Included in the Oslo Pass.

voyage.name: Astrup Fearnley Museet
voyage.price: Adult 120 kr, student 80 kr, children under 18 free; included in Oslo Pass
voyage.hours: Tue Wed Fri 12:00-17:00, Thu 12:00-19:00, Sat Sun 11:00-17:00, Mon closed
voyage.content: Astrup Fearnley Museet is a private collection of contemporary art, founded in 1993. The museum was relocated to Tjuvholmen, Aker Brygge in 2012. The building - designed by Renzo Piano - is spectacular in itself, and the museum offers a small green oasis with a beach, very welcome in the concrete surroundings of Aker Brygge. The museum offers temporary exhibitions, and is an established and central institution in Nor

voyage.name: National Museum
voyage.price: Adult 180 kr, seniors and people under 25 110 kr, free for children
voyage.content: This museum opened in 2022 and comprises the collections of the former National Gallery, the Museum of Architecture, the Museum of Decorative Arts and Design, and the Museum of Contemporary Art. The second floor houses paintings from the 15th century until today and includes a room exclusively dedicated to works from Edvard Munch while the other exhibits are displayed on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Oslo Transport Museum
voyage.content: The museum is in a former tram depot, and still has a track connecting to the Oslo tram system. It features a collection of old trams and buses. On the first Sunday afternoon of each month, the museum operates a historic tram in the streets.

voyage.name: Oscarshall
voyage.price: Adults 70 kr, seniors 60 kr, children 40 kr
voyage.content: Oscarshall is a royal summer Palace from the mid-19th century, now open to the public. A small palace filled with 19th-century Norwegian art and surrounded by a magnificent park. One of the finest examples of neo-gothic/romantic style in Norway. This small palace was never used as a residence. The Palace sits a hill above Frogner bay and offers fine panorama of the city. The palace was commissioned by Swedish-Norwegi

voyage.name: The Norwegian Museum of Cultural History
voyage.content: A large open air museum featuring typical buildings from various periods in Norwegian history. This includes a city building that shows living conditions from the 1850s to the 1980s. Included in the Oslo Pass.

voyage.name: Viking Ship Museum
voyage.price: 100 kr adult, 80 kr students and seniors, children under 18: free
voyage.content: In addition to two 1100-year-old Viking ships (apparently the best preserved in the world), it also contains various other Viking artefacts and a Viking burial chamber, complete with ancient skeletons. Included in the Oslo Pass. It is closed for a major refurbishment and plans to reopen in 2027.

voyage.name: Norwegian Maritime Museum
voyage.content: Houses a huge collection of ships and boats and records the impact of Norway's seafarers on their own country and the world. Included in the Oslo Pass.

voyage.name: Kon-Tiki Museum
voyage.content: Displays Thor Heyerdahl's balsa raft Kon-Tiki, and Ra II, as well as some other artefacts from Easter Island. Included in the Oslo Pass.

voyage.name: Fram-Museum
voyage.price: 180 kr adult; child, senior citizen and family tickets also available
voyage.content: Features the vessel Fram, the world's first ice breaker and the last polar expedition ship made of wood, and presents a history of polar exploration (with a strong Norwegian focus!) Included in the Oslo Pass.

voyage.name: The Holocaust Center
voyage.content: Also at Bygdøy, in the former residence of the Norwegian World War II collaborator and nationalist leader, Vidkun Quisling. The Center houses exhibitions and provides research on Holocaust and the plight of religious minorities. Included in the Oslo Pass.

voyage.name: Gustav Vigeland Museum
voyage.price: 80 kr adult. Included in the Oslo Pass
voyage.content: Situated to the south of the Frognerparken and Halvdan Svartes gate. The museum manages the sculptural works of Gustav Vigeland and offers a permanent exhibition of Gustav Vigelands sculptural works, as well as rolling exhibitions of various spatial art-forms (sculpture, installations and video-art). The museum was designed by Lorentz Ree and built in the 1920s. The striking building in red brick is one of the finest

voyage.name: Oslo Museum
voyage.content: Museum with exhibitions showing the city's cultural and commercial development. Free admission for everyone on the first Thursday of the month.

voyage.name: Frogner and Vigeland park
voyage.content: Frogner park including Vigeland Sculpture Park is a large green area about 10 minutes by subway from the city center. In addition to being a nice green recreational area, it is also decorated with hundreds of sculptures by the Norwegian artist Gustav Vigeland. There is a wonderfully relaxed atmosphere here, although the sculptures are a little disturbing. If your children want to climb the statues, nobody will even b

voyage.name: Nasjonalbiblioteket
voyage.content: Monumental building from 1913 with frescos by Emanuel Vigeland (younger brother of sculptor Gustav Vigeland). The Library holds copies of all published material in Norway. Fine retreat on a rainy day. Free entrance to Kartsenter (Map Center) with displays of map collections and history of geography and exploration in Norway. Cafe and bar within.

voyage.name: Henie Onstad Kunstsenter
voyage.content: The Henie Onstad Kunstsenter is an art museum located at Høvikodden (in Bærum municipality) on a fine location at the fjord near Sandvika. Sonja Henie and Niels Onstad created the museum by donating their private art collection and funds for running the museum. Henie was famous figure skater (three-time Olympic champion) and Hollywood film star. Onstad, her husband, was a shipping magnate and art collector. The museu

voyage.name: Huk beach
voyage.content: Beach, partly sandy, popular on warm summer days.

voyage.name: Vestkanttorget
voyage.content: Antiques and second hand market. Every Saturday on the corner of Professor Dahls gate and Neubergsgate at Frogner.

voyage.name: Frelsesarmeen (Salvation Army)
voyage.content: Salvation Army second-hand store done Norwegian style! Super high quality clothes, some furnishings, and a SA café/Sally Anne (SA's fair-trade concept store) right next door. Great place for inexpensive hats/gloves/socks when the Oslo winter sneaks up on you.

voyage.name: House of Oslo
voyage.content: A shopping centre focusing on interior designs with around 20 different shops with their own theme. This may be the most exquisite interior design centre in northern Europe. Illum Bolighus is especially worth a visit (this is a subsidiary of a famous Danish department store).

voyage.name: Aker Brygge
voyage.alt: continues over the bridge to Tjuvholmen
voyage.content: A seaside shopping and nightlife centre with high prices, but lots of glam and fun.

voyage.name: Krishna's Cuisine
voyage.content: Indian cuisine, vegetarian only.

voyage.name: Beach Club
voyage.content: Classical diner, opened 1989. Best burgers in town? Relaxed atmosphere, pleasant staff. Busy during summer. Hip, timeless and family friendly, all at the same time.

voyage.name: Curry and Ketchup
voyage.content: Cheap and popular Indian restaurant, often full during the weekends. Cash only.

voyage.name: Gate of India
voyage.content: Good Indian restaurant.

voyage.name: Pizza da Mimmo
voyage.content: Vying with Oslo Ladegård and Villa Paradiso to have the best pizza in Oslo.

voyage.name: Lanternen
voyage.price: Three kinds of herring with bread: 80kr.
voyage.content: Salads, sandwiches. The herring is good.

voyage.name: Odonata
voyage.content: Enjoy this unique design experience. This was the Oslo airport in the 1950s and is now a café with a great lunch menu and various cakes and treats.

voyage.name: Tintin
voyage.content: Sushi and Korean dishes.

voyage.name: Mares
voyage.content: A French style seafood restaurant.

voyage.name: Lorry
voyage.content: Lorry is an institution in Parkveien, near the Palace and at the lower end of Hegdehaugsveien/Bogstadveien shopping street. It is a quirky mix of proper restaurant and bar. Originally a "brown" tavern that has been in operation since 1901. The menu includes hearty food, particularly before Christmas when traditional Norwegian Christmas food is served. Beer on tap and a wide selection of beer in bottles. Lorry is a pl

voyage.name: Bølgen & Moi
voyage.content: Modern restaurant in the Frogner district. There's another Bølgen & Moi on Tjuvholmen island at the waterfront.

voyage.name: Feinschmecker
voyage.content: A feast for everyone involved, except perhaps your wallet. Exquisite dining at corporate prices.

voyage.name: Galt
voyage.content: Exclusive food of Norwegian raw materials.

voyage.name: Hos Thea
voyage.content: A small place with outstanding food, small seasonal menu.

voyage.name: Palace Grill
voyage.content: Highly recommended gourmet restaurant where the menu changes daily according to the chef's mood and available ingredients. A ten-course meal costs about 850 kr per person. Only 23 seats and no reservations, but a good bar to while away the hours waiting for food.

voyage.name: Lofoten fiskerestaurant
voyage.content: An exclusive fish restaurant serving fish, fish soup and shellfish.

voyage.name: Supreme Roastworks
voyage.content: Commonly quoted as one of the best coffee shops in Oslo, this half café, half Porsche show room serves coffee at a reasonable price.

voyage.name: Beer Palace
voyage.content: A popular pub with fair selection of Norwegian and foreign beers. In addition to enjoying good beer it's possible to play darts and get a slice of pizza. Every Monday an international beer course is held here by Ølakademiet.

voyage.name: The Pub Majorstuen
voyage.content: The pub for real beer connoisseurs and beer lovers, many types of specialty beer on tap.

voyage.name: Palace Grill
voyage.content: In addition to the gourmet restaurant (see above) the palace also includes a separate bar with nice drinks and concerts every Monday, plus the 3-story outdoor seating area "Skaugum" with lots of concert during summer.

voyage.name: Champagneria
voyage.content: Spanish cava and tapas bar, fairly cheap and enjoyable.

voyage.name: Oslo Mikrobryggeri
voyage.content: the first microbrewery in Scandinavia, over 35 beers on tap.

voyage.name: Highbury
voyage.content: Official Arsenal supporter pub in Norway.

voyage.name: Sollihagen & Nox
voyage.content: Sollihagen: This outdoor terrace has heat lamps and a South European party atmosphere. Nox: Exclusive indoor nightclub where you can book a table throughout the night. Age limit 20 on Thursday/Friday and 23 on Saturday.

voyage.name: Cochs Pensjonat
voyage.content: Centrally located, next to the Royal Palace and Slottsparken. Three types of room to meet all budgets. They don't serve breakfast but have agreement with a cafe nearby.

voyage.name: Clarion Collection Hotel Gabelshus
voyage.content: Quiet area. Breakfast, afternoon sweets and an evening meal are allways included.

voyage.name: Saga Hotel Oslo
voyage.content: Considering the hotel's fashionable location and spacious rooms, great value for money.

voyage.name: Scandic Sjølyst
voyage.content: 5 minutes by train from Oslo S central train station, by the E18 highway to the city. Scenic surroundings.

voyage.name: Scandic Solli
voyage.content: Central west end hotel with gym, sauna and conference facilities.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Gyldenlove
voyage.content: Renovated hotel, with excellent location in Oslo's west quarter, right in the city's best shopping avenue, Bogstadveien.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Vika Atrium
voyage.content: Central conference hotel.

voyage.name: Eyja Guldsmeden Hotel
voyage.content: 50 rooms, small but good value. Restaurant with Japanese food.

voyage.name: The Thief
voyage.content: On the water front of the Oslo Fjord in the middle of the business and contemporary art district of Oslo. The hotel is surrounded by many nice (and pricey) restaurants.

voyage.name: Aker river
voyage.content: Akerselva is Oslo's main river as it flows from Maridalen lake (Oslo's main water reservoir) to the fjord near the Central station. Previously Oslo's industrial heartland, now the river and its shores is converted into a green corridor almost the entire length from Grünerløkka to Maridalen. Bicycle and pedestrian paths along. Several small waterfalls. Industrial facilities remain as memories of Oslo's manufacturing o

voyage.name: Government Building Complex
voyage.content: Regjeringskvartalet is a group of buildings housing several of the offices of the executive branch (ministries) as well as the Supreme Court. The area does not display a consistent style but instead reflects 200 years of development. The prime minister's building and the Y-building are functionalist or brutalist architecture. The Y-building has a particular layout and the facade is decorated by Picasso's drawings car

voyage.name: Høyesterett
voyage.content: This monumental building hosts the High (or Supreme) Court of Norway. The Court was established in 1815 and has been in function since except for the occupation 1940-1945. Guided tours by appointment.

voyage.name: DogA - The Norwegian Centre for Design and Architecture
voyage.content: A thriving design and architecture centre providing areas for large and small exhibitions, conferences and meetings, activities for children, as well as a bookshop and café.

voyage.name: Kunstnernes hus
voyage.content: This 1931 building includes gallery and cafe. A prominent example of functionalism in Norway at the transition from neoclassicism.

voyage.name: Vår Frelsers Cemetery
voyage.content: Graves of Edvard Munch and Henrik Ibsen, and a large number of reputed Norwegians. Several statues, including one by Gustav Vigeland. Gamle Aker Church (the oldest building in Oslo) stands in the northern corner of the graveyard. The graveyard is pretty park and within easy walk the very centre at Karl Johans gate/Akersgata.

voyage.name: Damstredet/Fredensborg
voyage.content: The steep Damstredet with traditional wooden houses. Towering on the hill above are the iconic Westye Egeberg blocks.

voyage.name: Labour Museum
voyage.content: Well-kept workers' dwellings, winding streets and old factory building from the early industrial history of Oslo. Here you also find schools, public pools and factories which also become an integral part of the museum experience.

voyage.name: St.Hanshaugen park
voyage.content: A delightful public park on the highest hill in central Oslo. Great view of the city and surroundings. 1000 meters easy walk from Karl Johan street along Akersgata-Ullevålsveien past Vår Frelsers Gravlund (cemetery). The park has also given name to this popular neighborhood and to the larger administrative district (borough) that includes major parts of central Oslo.

voyage.name: Stensparken
voyage.content: This charming park begins at Fagerborg Church (neo-Gothic, granite) and stretches for some 500 meters to a fine panorama point in the northern end. There is a café on the top. Stensparken is a good choice if nearby St. Hanshaugen park is too crowded. Just west of the park there is a line of stately town houses.

voyage.name: Tramway Museum
voyage.content: Displays the history of Oslo's trams, buses and metro. Among other things, a wooden tram from the Holmenkollen line and a trolleybus are exhibited.

voyage.name: Hjula weaving mill
voyage.content: This industrial complex is perhaps an unusual attraction, but the striking buildings at the waterfall in Akerselva (Aker river) are one interesting legacy of Oslo's manufacturing past. It was the first water powered weaving mill in Norway, and during the late 1800s the largest textile company in Norway. The factory operated for more than 100 years. The water-powered factories along Aker river was an important factor

voyage.name: Blindern Campus - University of Oslo
voyage.content: Blindern Campus is home to functionalist landmarks from 1920-1930s. The new (1999) library building at Blindern is an imposing building in black polished stone and glass, it stands out as a landmark among the pre-war buildings.

voyage.name: Aamot bridge
voyage.alt: Pedestrian suspension bridge, crossing the Akerselva river
voyage.content: One of the earliest chain hangers in Europe and the earliest in Norway, leading from the river side park, across the river to the park by the neighborhood of Grünerløkka.

voyage.name: Saint Olav's Cathedral
voyage.alt: The Roman Catholic main cathedral in Norway. Seat of the Roman Catholic diocese of Oslo
voyage.content: the first Norwegian Roman Catholic cathedral (from 1856) which was built after the Protestant Reformation. The cathedral has church services and masses in Norwegian and several other languages, including English, Spanish and Polish.

voyage.name: Old Aker Church
voyage.content: This modest, sturdy, Romanesque church is the oldest existing building in Oslo. Built around 1100. It is one of the few Norwegian churches built in traditional basilica shape (three parallel naves). The building sits on a small hill in the northern corner of Vår Frelsers graveyard. Old Aker church has its own grave yard built on terraces at the edge of the hill, the grave yard is a pretty park with fine panorama.

voyage.name: Trefoldighetskirken
voyage.content: The largest church in Oslo. A monumental building in neo-Gothic style, constructed in red brick. The nave is octagonal with a Greek cross superimposed. The church is centrally located next to the Ministry offices and Oslo public library.

voyage.name: Sagene Church
voyage.content: Beautiful and monumental church with several towers and spiers in gothic revival style. Consecrated in 1891.

voyage.name: St. Edmund's Church
voyage.content: St. Edmund's Church belongs to the Church of England. It's a small neogothic building in red and yellow brick beneath the Hammersborg hill near the Swedish and Catholic churches as well as ministry buildings.

voyage.name: Svenska Margaretakyrkan
voyage.content: The Margareta Church in Oslo belongs the Lutheran Church of Sweden. The building sits on the small Hammersborg hilltop next to Deichmanske (public library), Trinity Church, St Olavs catholic church. Ministry buildings are next door across street. St. Edmund's Church (anglican) is nearby down the hill.

voyage.name: Oslo Synagogue
voyage.content: The present building was erected 1920. Afterwards, except during World War II, it has been the most important gathering place for the Jewish community in Norway.

voyage.name: Ullevål Stadion
voyage.content: This is one of the largest sports arenas in Norway. It is home ground for the Norwegian national team in soccer and there the Norwegian cup final is played. There are shops inside the stands. Sometimes there are concerts and other events there. Then there is the least crowding on the metro from east to west, opposite afterwards.

voyage.name: Bislett Stadion
voyage.content: is one of the best known sports facilities in Oslo. Houses the annual athletics ExxonMobil Bislett Games.

voyage.name: University of Oslo
voyage.content: The University of Oslo is Norway's oldest and second largest university. The main campus is at Blindern where most buildings are in red brick, functionalist style. On campus there are student associations and dormitories, gyms, the meteorological institute and research institutes within an area of more than 1 square kilometer. The university hospital is next door on the other side of ring road 3. Botanical garden and

voyage.name: Big Dipper
voyage.content: The best selection of vinyl LPs in Oslo! Pop/Rock, Indie, Soul, Metal/Hardrock, Jazz, Punk, Garagerock, Hip-hop, Blues, Country, Electronica and Reggae. Also a fine seletion of CDs in most genres.

voyage.name: Mathallen
voyage.content: Huge selection of exclusive international and traditional Norwegian food in this new indoor market, and serving of food and drinks.

voyage.name: Baby Shop AS
voyage.content: One of Oslo's oldest and most traditional baby stores. It is famous for its celebrity shoppers like the Princess of Norway Märtha Louise and the Crown Princess Mette-Marit.

voyage.name: Bogstadveien
voyage.content: Good for non-chain stores, focus on clothes and accessories.

voyage.name: Valkyrien Take Away
voyage.content: Their burgers are famous. Limited seating, but there is a very small park close to it where you can enjoy your food.

voyage.name: Hai Cafe
voyage.content: Good fried or fresh spring rolls, tasty duck breast hoi sin sauce with pac choi. In general tasty and cheap.

voyage.name: Bari
voyage.content: Inventive name for a pizza joint, the best in the area.

voyage.name: Dalat Kafe
voyage.content: Vietnamese. Simple interior but very popular among people who appreciate authentic Vietnamese food. Dishes and beverages at affordable prices.

voyage.name: Marino
voyage.content: Generally accepted as the best kebab in the area, but steadily contested by Mediterran and Lille Amir.

voyage.name: Lille Saigon Kafe
voyage.content: The first of the Vietnamese bargain offerings are still going strong. Although the food in Vietnam is known to be tastier, you'll need a plane ticket to Hanoi to get it this cheap! (at least it feels like that when you're used to Norwegian food prices).

voyage.name: Tay Do Cafe
voyage.content: Vietnamese. Try the 'Dagens' (daily special) for only about 80kr, or some of their other Vietnamese offerings.

voyage.name: Mitsu
voyage.content: Japanese/Asian. Probably the best budget sushi in town, as well as baguettes (from NOK30) and a few hot dishes. Not the most cosy place to eat, but a great place for a cheap lunch or dinner.

voyage.name: Bislett Kebab
voyage.content: Voted Oslo's best for kebabs many times, not the cheapest place, but good value for money. However if you want authentic kebabs try Torggata or the beginning of Trondheimsveien.

voyage.name: Tasty Thai
voyage.content: Oslo's best budget Thai offering.

voyage.name: University of Oslo Student Canteen (Fredrikke)
voyage.content: Student canteen food at student prices. Several canteens dish up filling food at budget prices, the main canteen in the Fredrikke building has edible meals at under 50kr. There's also several other student canteens, although they are closed during the summer. One branch in the city centre is at St. Olavs plass.

voyage.name: Vegan Loving Hut Oslo
voyage.content: Vegetarian restaurant, with exciting and tasty dishes from around the world. Take-away-service.

voyage.name: Funky Fresh Foods
voyage.content: Genuine vegetarian food in unique architectural space, overlooking the Aker River.

voyage.name: Arakataka
voyage.content: The most upmarket offering in Oslo's Bermuda Triangle of cheap eating, Arakataka manages to pull off decent Nordic, French and Mediterranean cuisine at decent prices. Small dishes; it takes three dishes or more to get saturated.

voyage.name: Elvebredden
voyage.content: Inside the Design and Architecture centre, Elvebredden has some fantastic lunch offerings and stunning, but fairly upmarket, main dishes in the evening.

voyage.name: Intermezzo
voyage.content: East-Asian and sushi.

voyage.name: Lorry
voyage.content: traditional restaurant with a restaurant menu based on the traditional Norwegian cuisine. Widely used as a meeting place and a drinking den .

voyage.name: Schrøder
voyage.content: Dark drinking den with traditional, inexpensive and fattening Norwegian food. Featured in Jo Nesbø's novels.

voyage.name: St. Lars
voyage.content: Fish or meat barbecue from charcoal grill.

voyage.name: Delhi Tandoori Restaurant
voyage.content: Looks scruffy from the outside, but don't let that fool you. A fantastic Indian restaurant with all the trimmings.

voyage.name: Restaurant Mother India
voyage.content: Popular, authentic Indian restaurant

voyage.name: Lorry
voyage.content: Restaurant and traditional venue for cultural personalities. The menu is inspired by the Norwegian and European cuisine. There is a rich selection of beer and wine.

voyage.name: Teddy's Soft Bar
voyage.content: Established in 1958, this is the only bar in Oslo that's protected by cultural authorities, due to its true 1950s setting with original interior. This is where the rockabilly cats and kittens hang out and low-key rock and film stars lurk in the corners. Teddy's brought milk shakes to Norway, but sadly they've stopped serving those. They do serve beer, wine, spirits, soft drinks and various coffee drinks. And you can

voyage.name: Robinet
voyage.content: A little gem of a bar that serves some of the best drinks in town. It's not much more than a hole in the wall, so don't expect to get a seat. The bartenders (who are often a bit moody, so no music requests!) play everything from free jazz to krautrock to gangsta-rap on the sound system.

voyage.name: Crowbar
voyage.content: Crowbar has 20 beers on tap, 5 of them made by them.

voyage.name: Cafe Sara
voyage.address: corner of Torggata and Hausmanns gate.
voyage.content: Conveniently close to Anker Hostel, Cafe Sara pours beer and dishes up tasty Turkish and Mexican dishes for not too much money. Great outdoor seating. Very nice pub with a great atmosphere and well known for its cheap but great food and large selection of craft beers.

voyage.name: Verkstedet
voyage.content: Nice rock bar with a cosy and great backyard which it shares with Cafe Sara. The club has a stage, where local and foreign acts appear. At the weekends the club transforms into a rock disco, where you can dance to great rock music. The bar dishes up with great cocktails and unlimited amounts of beer, both on tap and bottles.

voyage.name: Tekehtopa
voyage.content: Lovely cafe serving beer, wine, drinks and small dishes in a fabulous former pharmacy. (Tekehtopa spelled backwards, apotheket, means "the pharmacy" in Norwegian.) One of the prettiest cafes around! Adjoined by Bar Babylon, an industrial-style club with wonderful back yard seating.

voyage.name: Blå
voyage.content: Be sure to check their event calendar, every week they have concerts with a variety of international and Norwegian bands and/or DJs. Each Sunday there is a free jazz/blues/soul concert. Walk up the river from the centre and you'll find it. Old factory style houses with lots of graffiti.

voyage.name: Rockefeller/John Dee and Sentrum Scene
voyage.content: Some of Oslo's best stages for music. Rockefeller houses three stages while Sentrum Scene houses a fourth and larger stage. Mostly concert stages but they also show the odd football match or cinema. Both Norwegian and international artists.

voyage.name: Revolver
voyage.content: Rock pub with most of Oslo's hipsters lurking in the corners. Not too expensive, and quite an extensive choice of beers on tap.

voyage.name: Anker Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm: kr 230-290, Double: kr 620-640, Bed linen: kr 50
voyage.content: 290 beds. Very centrally located, 5 minutes walk to the central station or Grünerløkka.

voyage.name: Anker Hotel
voyage.alt: Don't confuse with the neighboring hostel
voyage.price: Single: kr 631-785, Double: kr 685-785, Family-5 single beds: kr 1,547
voyage.content: All rooms have TV, free wi-fi and bathroom with shower. Rich breakfast is included.

voyage.name: Comfort Hotel Xpress Youngstorget
voyage.price: Double: For 2 nights or more: 695kr per night
voyage.content: Centrally located, 5 minutes walk from Karl Johans gate and Oslo Central Station (Oslo S)

voyage.name: P:S Hotel
voyage.content: A relatively small hotel within a short walk to the more vibrant Grünerløkka. Intimate and cozy.

voyage.name: Scandic Holberg Hotel
voyage.price: Prices vary by season, see official website
voyage.content: Affordable bed & breakfast hotel, centrally located, not far from Oslo's main thoroughfare, Karl Johans Gate.

voyage.name: Scandic St. Olav's plass
voyage.content: Modern rooms and award-winning breakfast.

voyage.name: Scandic Vulcan
voyage.content: Relatively newly built hotel just off the river.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Munch
voyage.content: A short walk to the main street, as well as easy walking distance to public transportation, airport shuttle bus and a vast variety of shops, restaurants, museums and theatres.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Rosenkrantz
voyage.content: Popular hotel close to downtown (Sentrum).

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Slottsparken
voyage.content: The hotel is located on the quiet side of the park.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Ullevål Stadion
voyage.price: Prices vary by season, see official website
voyage.content: Parking garage for hotel guests in the basement, 10 minutes by metro to Oslo S train station.

voyage.name: Kampen
voyage.content: The Kampen neighbourhood is an area with many traditional wooden houses.

voyage.name: Barcode
voyage.content: Barcode defines a new waterfront in the Bjørvika area. The plan for the new structures was adopted in 2003, and as of 2015 nine buildings are finished, and two are under construction. Three more are planned. While the buildings contribute to a spectacular waterfront, viewed from the seaside, they also block much of the sea-view from the other side, and therefore their contribution to the concept of "Fjordbyen", the i

voyage.name: Popsenteret
voyage.hours: Mon closed, Tue Wed Fri 10:00-16:00, Thu 10:00-19:00, Sat Sun 11:00-17:00
voyage.content: Popsenteret (Center of Popular Music) is a museum and location for various events and rolling exhibitions, interactions, etc., within the cultural realm of pop music.

voyage.name: Munch Museum
voyage.price: Adult 160 kr, student 100 kr, child free
voyage.content: Opened in Oct 2021, this striking harbour building exhibits paintings by the Norwegian painter Edward Munch (1863-1944). Lots of his famous work is here - he made many versions of "The Scream" and these are rotated for display. Munch also produced huge paintings for the grandiose walls of the University of Oslo Aula, but these are seldom accessible to the public. Entrance is free on Wednesdays from 6pm-9pm, you still

voyage.name: Rodeløkka wooden houses
voyage.content: Traditional Norwegian wood architecture, not found downtown anymore.

voyage.name: Akrobaten pedestrian bridge
voyage.content: Contemporary 200-m-long pedestrian bridge across the tracks of Oslo central station, connecting Grønland, where the Barcode high rises are, and Bjørvika, where the Opera House is. Awarded 1st price (Certificate of Excellence) in ECCS, European Award for Steel Bridges, in 2012. Popular spot for photo shoots, day and night.

voyage.name: Torshov
voyage.content: Torshov is the neighbourhood North of Grünerløkka, uphill from ring road 2. The central parts of Torshov was a large housing project in the city of Oslo in the 1920s. As a residential area, Torshov has a characteristic monumental design with elements of baroque revival and neo-classical style. The layout was inspired by the English garden city movement and the area was basically greenfield in the 1920s. The Torshov b

voyage.name: Walk along the river Akerselva
voyage.content: An 8-km-long walk totally takes you past forested areas, historical buildings, fishing and swimming spots and several waterfalls.

voyage.name: Sunday Market at Birkelunden
voyage.alt: east end - near junction of Toftes Gate and Seilduksgata
voyage.content: Antiques and second hand market every Sunday noon until 7PM at Birkelunden park at Grünerløkka.

voyage.name: Ekebergmarkedet
voyage.content: Flea market and one of Northern Europe's largest swapmeet/markets for vintage car and bike parts. Takes place early May and mid. September at the north-west part of Ekeberg Park. Arranged by Norsk Veteranvogn Klubb (http://veteranvogn.no)

voyage.name: Intility Arena
voyage.alt: Home ground for the best football club in Oslo, Vålerenga Fotball
voyage.content: Don't miss a home game with Norway's most passionate football fans.The stadium bar/restaurant has good burgers and a selection of craft beer.

voyage.name: Sørenga
voyage.content: Fjord pool with seawater from the Oslofjord. Swimming pool, children's pool, beach and a large recreational area. Crowded on sunny summer days. If it's not tempting to swim, take a stroll anyway along the scenic waterfront where there are outdoor areas and new cafes and restaurants.

voyage.name: Tøyenbadet
voyage.content: Norway's most popular public pool. All-year: two indoor swimming pools, diving board, waterslide, in the summer: two outdoor pools.

voyage.name: Botanical Garden
voyage.alt: tram 17 or bus 31 to Lakkegata skole or t-bane to Tøyen, walking distance 200 metres
voyage.content: The University botanical gardens is located just south of Tøyen park next door to Munch Museum. A wonderful and relaxing area. Free entrance, opening hours Apr-Sep: Sa Su 10:00-20:00, M-F 07:00-20:00; Oct-Mar: Sa Su 10:00-17:00, M-F 07:00-17:00.

voyage.name: Middelalderparken
voyage.content: Ruins of medieval old town of Oslo, such as church ruins and ruins of the former Royal Estate. Location of the annual rock music festival Øyafestivalen.

voyage.name: Birkelunden
voyage.content: A cool park in eastern Oslo, the uppermost park in Grünerløkka neighbourhood, a so-called Greenwich village look-alike area. On Sundays, there is a second-hand market. The name refers to the birch threes there. The park covers one block.

voyage.name: Olaf Ryes plass
voyage.content: A small square park in eastern Oslo, Grünerløkka neighborhood, a so-called Greenwich village look-alike area. The park covers exactly one block in Grünerløkka's grid.

voyage.name: Sofienbergparken
voyage.content: (The largest of the parks in Grünerløkka) A lot of activities all day long and especially on weekends; ball-playing, picnics, public barbecues, especially nice area for children.

voyage.name: Ekebergparken
voyage.content: At the steep, green hill east of city centre (tram 18 or 19 to Ekebergparken, bus 34 or 74 to Brannfjellveien) is even a sculpture park, with works by Norwegian and international artists such as Salvador Dalí, Lynn Chadwick, Richard Hudson and Per Ung among others. This point is assumed to be the background for Scream, Edvard Munch's famous picture. Alongside the idyllic forest paths you can see sculptures, but also

voyage.name: Torshovparken
voyage.content: A fine park on a hill top in the middle of the classical Torshov neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Torshovdalen
voyage.content: Big park in a small valley between Torshov and road 4. Popular for skiing in Winter. The city of Oslo maintains cross-country trails when there is enough snow. Skateboard facilities at the lower end.

voyage.name: Grünerløkka
voyage.content: In this area you will find lower prices and more intense nightlife and items for sale than otherwise in Oslo.

voyage.name: Helvete
voyage.content: This was a record shop run by Euronymous (the stage name for Øystein Aarseth, considered to be a very central figure in the early black metal scene) between 1991 and 1993. It was a meeting place for the members of the early scene. As of 2022, the building houses Neseblod Records, which maintains the place as an unofficial museum to black metal.

voyage.name: Sandaker senter
voyage.content: Shopping center indoors

voyage.name: Storo storsenter
voyage.content: One of the largest and busiest indoor shopping centers in the city of Oslo.

voyage.name: Grønlands Torg
voyage.content: Many cultures and nationalities are represented, both by customers and by those who work there. The mall is especially known for the great selection of fruits and vegetables from Norway and distant countries. There are also shoe, clothing and fabric stores there and several eateries.

voyage.name: Grønland Basar
voyage.content: What you can't find at Grønland Torg, you might find here.

voyage.name: Neseblod Records
voyage.content: Black Metal Shop and museum in Schweigaards gate in the same building in which Helvete was located in the early 1990s.

voyage.name: Punjab Tandoori
voyage.content: The friendliest Sikh in the world dishes out cheap, tasty Indian food from the microwave or stove. No real tandoor.

voyage.name: Sushi Deluxe
voyage.content: Great tasting sushi meals from as little as 79kr. Also have small daily specials for 59 kr (fried rice, fried noodles, etc.)

voyage.name: Tandoori Curry Corner
voyage.content: The neighbouring restaurant of the Punjab Tandoori is even cheaper, but the helpings are smaller and packs less of a punch.

voyage.name: L'Oasis Mazze
voyage.content: Bedouin-style restaurant run by Palestinians. Falafels, tagine, etc. Good for lunch or dinner. Friendly staff and low prices.

voyage.name: Tran Sushi & Wok
voyage.content: The restaurant offers good sushi for a nice price. Featuring about 10 seats, the place could be considered more a take-away than a restaurant.

voyage.name: Noahs Ark
voyage.content: It has some excellent Turkish dishes. Burgers, pizza and breakfast are also available from 49 kr and upwards. A cosy place with occasional unexpected classical music played early in the day.

voyage.name: Oslo Ladegård
voyage.content: Fighting it out with Villa Paradiso and Pizza da Mimmo to provide the city's best Italian pizza.

voyage.name: Smia
voyage.content: Atmospheric restaurant in an old wooden house area with tons of charm.

voyage.name: Kampen Bistro
voyage.content: Lovely neighbourhood joint with brilliant food and occasional free concerts.

voyage.name: Olympen / Lompa
voyage.content: One of the best known and largest places in east Oslo. Restaurant, beer Hall, nightclub and roof terrace. With classic Norwegian food.

voyage.name: Le Benjamin
voyage.content: French bistro at the south part of Grünerløkka with relaxed atmosphere and good food.

voyage.name: Villa Paradiso
voyage.content: Excellent Italian pizza at Grünerløkka. Children friendly.

voyage.name: Mucho Mas
voyage.content: Cal-mex joint offering huge meals, but reports say quality has faded. A new branch near the crossing of Hegdehaugsveien/Sporveisgata in Homansbyen (tram 11-19 to Rosenborg) does little to redeem this.

voyage.name: Karlsborg Spiseforretning
voyage.alt: In a scenic venue, built in 1863
voyage.content: Serving traditional Norwegian dishes, near the entrance to the sculpture park.

voyage.name: Villa Paradiso Lilleborg
voyage.content: Cafe and pizzeria in Lilleborg area at Aker river. In one of the previous factory buildings converted to cafes, theater and residences. Lilleborg was a soap factory established in mid 1800s.

voyage.name: Ekebergrestauranten
voyage.content: An architectural monument, this place offers gourmet dining and Oslo's best views. Hugely popular but the service can disappoint.

voyage.name: Maaemo
voyage.price: 1250 kr for 9-course menu, add 1050 kr for the drink pairing menu
voyage.content: This New Nordic Cuisine restaurant serving organic, local food jumped straight to two stars in Michelin's Guide Rouge at the earliest opportunity after opening, the first Nordic restaurant to do so. They have now advanced to three stars. World class restaurant.

voyage.name: Nodee
voyage.content: All-Asian gourmet offering south of downtown, at the waterfront. The best East-Asian restaurant in Northern Europe (competing it out with dinner), with prices to match. There are two restaurants: Barcode, and Sky. Sky is on the thirteenth floor, and is more of a bar/lounge; while Barcode is the main restaurant.

voyage.name: Lincoln Gastro Pub
voyage.content: A pleasant English football pub with outdoor seating and smokehouse in the backyard. Also serves food.

voyage.name: Zen Spiseri og Cafebar
voyage.content: A mysteriously stylish interior for a dive bar, dishing out some of Oslo's cheaper beer. Laid-back, relaxing atmosphere, usually draws a somewhat older crowd. Small menu with passable food.

voyage.name: Bar Boca
voyage.content: The teeny-weeny Bar Boca is the place to go in Oslo if you fancy an innovative and memorable cocktail. Owner Jan Vardøen has become something of a local legend for his mixing skills and his intimate little bar has become a destination for those serious about their drink. This warm cosy bar, with its low-key 1950s décor, may be matchbox sized, with just five tables, but it's the drinks that rule here and they won't le

voyage.name: Aku-Aku Tiki Bar
voyage.content: Another of Jan Vardøens successful cocktail bars, Easter Island style. Let Voo-Doo-Mary-Lou knock you out surrounded by bamboo, blowfish and Thor Heyerdahl, after a long day at the Kontiki-museum. Cool and cozy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Cafe Stolen
voyage.content: Indian cuisine and cheap beer in an informal setting. No name on the door, just a chair hanging from above the door (hence the name 'the chair').

voyage.name: Parktheateret
voyage.content: Bar with indoor and outdoor seating. Concert hall indoors in a former cinema.

voyage.name: Grünerløkka Brygghus
voyage.content: Grünerløkka Brygghus has 10 or more of their own beers on tap, with some others. They also serve food.

voyage.name: Oslo Ocean Bar
voyage.content: A neighbourhood bar with customers, mostly returning, at every time of the day (from 08:00). The staff is great! The service is impeccable despite the low prices and the very unpretentious surroundings (and clientele).

voyage.name: Schouskjelleren
voyage.content: Microbrewery in the basement of the former larger Schous brewery;13 beers on tap; about half are house-made.

voyage.name: Südøst
voyage.content: A short walk from the Anker hostel, this place has become quite fashionable. Lovely outdoor seating, great (but a tad expensive) food and a marvellous dining room.

voyage.name: Stargate
voyage.content: Meeting place just east of Akerselva river.

voyage.name: Andy's Pub
voyage.content: English style pub. Football matches on big screen.

voyage.name: Pigalle
voyage.content: Cocktail bar with history dating back to 1965. Original interior.

voyage.name: Ruinen Bar & Café
voyage.content: Have a cooling drink or play billiard. Occasionally concerts.

voyage.name: St. Halvards Pub & Bistro
voyage.content: A typical neighbourhood pub with a simple menu and occasionally live music in Oslo's Old Town.

voyage.name: No. 53
voyage.content: Café, pub and cocktail bar, live music.

voyage.name: Enga Pub
voyage.content: Beautiful Vålerenga is like a village in the city. In this neighborhood, everyone supports the same football team, Vålerenga FK, the best soccer club in Oslo. The pub is the venue for the most eager supporters and the home arena is close to this neighborhood.

voyage.name: Ekeberg Camping
voyage.price: 2-person tent: kr 185, 4-person tent with car: kr 270
voyage.content: Open Jun–Aug. The closest campsite to central Oslo. Beautiful view of the city. No cabins. Owned by the Norwegian Automobile Federation. Mini-golf and horse rental. Fully equipped sanitary facilities: showers with hot and cold water, toilets, kitchen, launderette.

voyage.name: Oslo Hotel Apartments
voyage.content: This has a range of room options, from one bed in a 6-person dorm, to hotel style rooms.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel Nydalen
voyage.content: Choose from funky "Chilli" or more staid "Urban" rooms

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Storo
voyage.price: Prices vary by season, see official website
voyage.content: One of the newest hotels in the city of Oslo, Conference facilities and gym. Also offers disabled-friendly rooms 10 minutes travel by metro to the Oslo S central train station, 6 minutes by tram to Grünerløkka.

voyage.name: Scandic Helsfyr
voyage.content: On the outskirts of the inner city, but still very central.

voyage.name: Holmenkollen
voyage.content: The ski jump located on the west side of Oslo, which was rebuilt for the World Ski Championships in 2011. It first opened in 1892 and has been re-built many times since then. It had more than 1 million visitors every year, and was one of the biggest tourist attractions in Norway. There is also the oldest ski museum in the world, opened in 1923. Walking and mountain bike riding are popular activities here during the s

voyage.name: Holmenkollen Chapel
voyage.content: built with inspiration from the stave churches and benefits from dragestil wood carvings. The chapel used by the Royal Family at Christmas time and Holmenkollen ski festival.

voyage.name: Emanuel Vigeland Museum
voyage.hours: Only open a few hours every Sun afternoon
voyage.content: Among Oslos best hidden secrets. Gustav Vigeland's not so well-known younger brother erected the building as a museum for his art in 1926, but later decided it should serve as a mausoleum, with his urn placed above the door. The main attraction in this museum with no windows is the 800 square meters fresco "Vita", (Italian for "life"), showing the human life from conception till death, but other examples of his art a

voyage.name: Norwegian Museum of Science and Technology & The Norwegian Telecommunications Museum
voyage.content: A fun and very interactive place for both children and adults. Contrary to information in the common tourist brochures this building.

voyage.name: Nordmarka (Oslo forest)
voyage.address: North of Oslo + eastern (Lillomarka), northern and western suburbs
voyage.content: Oslo is surrounded by wide and partly dense forests, generally known as Marka, of which Nordmarka is the largest and most accessible section (in addition to Nordmarka there similar areas east, south and west of the city). There are lots of roads and trails criss-crossing these wide forests, but no cars, only skiers, hikers and bicycles. So it is essentially the largest park in town. There are countless lakes, many ri

voyage.name: Sognsvann
voyage.content: Sognsvann lake is one of the most popular places in Marka (Oslo forest), nice meadows and easy path around lake, paths continue through the forest - metro line 5 to Sognsvann station. Surprisingly this lake is the geographical mid point of Oslo.

voyage.name: Stovnertårnet
voyage.content: A 265 meter long circular walkway leads to the top of the tower, designed in such a way for universal accessibility. Great views of the Oslo Fjord in the distance and the Groruddalen valley in low bird's eye view.

voyage.name: Swimming (outdoor, freshwater)
voyage.content: For fresh water swimming, Akerselva is considered clean north of Nydalen. The best spot may be at Frysja (bus 22-25-54 to Stillatorget). Don't forget that many of the lakes in "Oslomarka" are for swimming and recreation (Sognsvann lake for instance). Note that some major lakes (Maridalsvannet in particular) are drinking water for the city, restrictions on swimming and camping. Buy a map and bring your swimming gear!

voyage.name: Holmenkollen
voyage.content: The area around Holmenkollen (T-bane 1) is well suited for cross-country skiing, but also a nice area for hiking during summertime. While you are there, you can also visit the ski-museum which is located close to the ski-jump. For additional fun, buy a cheap sledge or "akebrett", or rent a proper one from Frognerseteren, and sleigh down from Frognerseteren to Midtstuen station. This was actually the venue of the slei

voyage.name: Oslo Climbingpark
voyage.alt: Climbing in outdoor trees, zips and on a climbing wall.
voyage.hours: See prices and opening hours April to October
voyage.content: Perfect for adults and teenagers who want to challenge themselves with expert guidance.

voyage.name: Oslo vinterpark
voyage.content: The capital's greatest ski resort for alpine skiing. Ski school and ski equipment rental. Dinig. After ski Fridays. Oslo Vinterpark offers multiple lifts and slopes stretching from the Tryvann Tower, at the top and all the way down to Sørkedalen, where the 1300m Wyllerløypa ends. See weather forecast.

voyage.name: Oslo Summerpark
voyage.content: To adults and children: challenge yourself, swing through the trees, fun zip lines, balancing along a section of posts. The Climbing Park is designed and constructed so that trees can grow to their natural shape and size. Routes and paths are placed naturally using the latest technology and an independent arborist that puts safety first. Knowledgeable training.

voyage.name: Stovner Senter
voyage.content: One of the largest shopping centers in City of Oslo, located in the northeastern tip.

voyage.name: Grorud Senter
voyage.content: Shopping center, located centrally in the Grorud district.

voyage.name: Vindern torvet
voyage.content: Shopping center along the Holmenkollen line.

voyage.name: IKEA Furuset
voyage.price: Hotdogs for 5kr and pizza slices for 15kr.
voyage.content: Shop for furniture and eat cheaply!

voyage.name: Egon Ullevål
voyage.content: Serves nice food for a fair price/quality ratio. All kinds of dishes available, you do need to go to the bar to order

voyage.name: Frognerseteren Restaurant
voyage.content: -is a dragestil complex consisting of patisserie Seterstua and restaurant Finstua as well as banqueting facilities. Wonderful views over the entire city. The food is based on Norwegian cuisine traditions, but is expensive.

voyage.name: Anexet Sportsbar
voyage.content: Neighborhood bar with football on both large screen and flat screen. Occasionally jazz concerts. Sushi dining, or as a take away.

voyage.name: Bogstad Camping
voyage.price: 2-person tent: kr 185, 4-person tent with car: kr 270, Cabin: kr 500-1290
voyage.content: Bogstad has cabins and tent space. Close to the campsite there is a mini-mart Kiwi (used by the locals), a petrol station Statoil with heat-up fast food options, and a fast food restaurant Jafs! which does pizzas, kebabs and burgers ("Hamburger meny" take-away, 100g burger & French fries & salad & drink, kr 95).

voyage.name: Haraldsheim Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm: kr 255-280, Double: kr 610-690, Bed linen: kr 50, Breakfast included, 10% discount with HI membership
voyage.content: The biggest HI hostel in Oslo. Not too far from the action (but it is hard to find), walking distance to the lively neighbourhoods of Torshov and Grünerløkka. Located in a very quiet area of Oslo, this is a place you'd go to sleep, not to party. The breakfast is outstanding for a hostel and is vegan-friendly, although with reduced choice. It is advisable to reconfirm your booking before you come and inform at what ti

voyage.name: Oslo Hostel Rønningen
voyage.price: Dorm: from kr 230, 10% discount with HI membership
voyage.content: Open June 1 - August 19. 7.5 km from the center.

voyage.name: Olympiatoppen Sportshotell
voyage.content: Peacefully located on the edge of the forest Nordmarka.

voyage.name: Quality Hotel™ 33
voyage.content: A conference hotel with 242 hotel rooms and 17 conference rooms. Panoramic views from the upper floors.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel & Conference Center, Oslo Alna
voyage.content: Comfortable hotel and conference facilities. Well-equipped fitness room.

voyage.name: Scandic Holmenkollen Park Hotel
voyage.content: Close to the skiing facilities at Holmenkollen, this is a hotel built in the classical Norwegian dragon style.

voyage.name: Soria Moria Hotell
voyage.content: The name is taken from a castle in Asbjørnsen and Moe's folk tales. Spectacular views from above the city and close to forest and ski facilities.

voyage.name: Thon Hotel Linne
voyage.content: Located in a suburb, not very far from the offices and commercial business districts of Helsfyr and Økern.

voyage.name: Lysebu
voyage.content: Historic hotel in the forest, located over the city and close to the Holmenkollen ski facilities and hiking areas. Used for conferences, celebrations, honeymoons and weddings. Traditional Norwegian building style in timber.

voyage.name: Ekebergsletta
voyage.content: A field and a park system, neighbor to Ekebergparken Sculpture Park.The forest area fits to go hiking in. Don't forget a picnic basket. The field is used primarily for sporting events and is the location for Norway Cup, the world’s largest annually football tournament for children and young people aged 10 to 19 years old. At the northern edge of the hill there are spectacular views of the city.

voyage.name: Østmarka
voyage.content: A large forest area with idyllic trails and small lakes that the locals use for recreation, hiking (summer) and cross-country skiing (winter). See map.

voyage.name: Lambertseter Swimming Pool
voyage.content: Indoors swimming pool open to the public on weekends. Swimwear for sale.

voyage.name: Holmlia Senter
voyage.content: Shopping centre close to the railway station.

voyage.name: Lambertseter Senter
voyage.content: Shopping centre close to Lambertseter subway station, line 1 or 4.

voyage.name: Senter Syd Mortensrud
voyage.content: Shopping centre close to the terminal station for subway line 3.

voyage.name: Sæter
voyage.content: Shopping centre close to Sæter tram stop.

voyage.name: Burger King
voyage.content: Chain. Hamburgers & other fast food

voyage.name: Lambertseter Kro
voyage.content: Serves Chinese food. Take-away-service.

voyage.name: Egon Nordstrand
voyage.content: The first restaurant in this chain. Serves nice food for a much better price/quality ratio. All kinds of dishes available, you do need to go to the bar to order.

voyage.name: Langøyene Island
voyage.content: Not an official campsite; however, Langøyene Island is the only island in the inner part of the Oslo fjord that allows free camping (tents only). You may only stay 2 days unless you have special permission. You must keep the island clean. Police have their own boats and enforce these laws via hefty fines.

voyage.name: Sørmarka hotell
voyage.content: Venue hotel in the forest.

voyage.name: Quality Hotel™ Entry
voyage.content: is situated at Kolbotn in stunning natural surroundings. Hiking trails and cycling routes that easily enable you to reach nearby locations such as the wonderful beach at Hvervenbukta (Oslo).

voyage.name: Oscarsborg
voyage.content: Hotel in Oscarsborg fortress.
